description.before: A modular predator-prey model demonstrating the classic snowshoe hare and Canadian lynx population cycles. The model uses graphical functions to capture non-linear relationships between hare density and both lynx mortality and kill rates. Based on the classic Lotka-Volterra dynamics but with more realistic functional responses. Reference: Lotka, A. J. (1920). Analytical note on certain rhythmic relations in organic systems. PNAS, 6(7), 410-415. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.6.7.410
description.after: Source-backed scalar flattening of Bobby Powers's modular Stella hares/lynxes teaching example. Restores the two original clamped graphical functions; the preserved Euler default matches the original 25-row canonical output. The original nonnegative stock/flow constraints are not represented by this scalar engine, so arbitrary scenarios are not a complete semantic reproduction. Not field-calibrated ecological prediction.

reference.after: Powers, B. (2015). Hares and lynxes modular Stella model, SDXorg/test-models, revision 21aab02739dc5187bc9564e4d3de14e575905d2f. Default canonical output from Stella 10.0.6.

description.before: A model demonstrating the 'capability trap' - a common management archetype where organizations sacrifice long-term capability for short-term performance. When faced with pressure, managers often 'work harder' rather than 'work smarter', reducing time spent on improvement activities. This creates a reinforcing feedback loop: reduced capability leads to lower performance, which increases pressure, further reducing improvement time. Reference: NSIDC Arctic Sea Ice News. Source: https://nsidc.org/arcticseaicenews/
description.after: Restored PySD-Cookbook Capability Trap teaching equations and three original clamped graphical functions. All original local nodes, inputs and layout are retained. The source itself warns that its working-time formulation is not quite correct and conflates pressures and improvement time; this caveat is retained rather than silently corrected. Source-equation reconstruction is not empirical calibration or scientific certification.

description.before: A workforce dynamics model showing how organizations balance hiring rookies with the need for expert supervision. Demonstrates the organizational learning challenge where new hires require supervision from experts, reducing expert capacity for productive work. Features feedback between task backlog pressure and hiring decisions. Reference: Cachon, G., & Terwiesch, C. (2012). Matching Supply with Demand. McGraw-Hill. Source: https://www.mheducation.com/
description.after: Restored PySD-Cookbook Rookies Demo Model teaching equations and its original clamped hiring-response table. Source punctuation in hour variables is mapped explicitly. The source directly limits task completion rate by backlog, a dimensional assumption retained for fidelity; no extra positivity or hiring rules are invented. Constants, units and organizational realism remain uncalibrated.
